rows.speaker: رسول الله صلى الله عليه وسلم
rows.claim: At Uhud, Qazman fought fiercely although the Prophet said he belonged to the people of Hell; wounded, he said he fought only for tribal zeal, then severed his hand and died.
rows.anchor: ومأن رسول الله صلى الله عليه وسلم : ( إنه من أهل النار , فجرح فبشر بالجنة فقال : واللهما قاتلت إلاحمية لقومي

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The passage names al-Jadd ibn Qays, who asked to be excused lest he be tempted, and identifies Ibn Ubayy as the head of the hypocrites who gathered around him.
rows.anchor: والجد بن قيس وهو الذي قال : ( ائذن لي ولاتفتني ) وعبد الله بن أبي رأس المنافقين وإليه كانوا يجتمعون

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The author associates Wadiʿa al-ʿAwfi, Malik ibn Abi Fawqal, Suwayd, and Daʿis with Ibn Ubayy's group and cites the revelation about hypocrites siding with their disbelieving scripture-community brothers.
rows.anchor: وفيه وفي وديعة العوفي ومالك بن أبي فوقل وسويد وداعس وهم من رهطه نزل

rows.speaker: الحرالي
rows.claim: Feigning alignment with both sides under the guise of prudence is corruption; the hypocrite is neither a loyal friend nor an open enemy, so one cannot trust him.
rows.anchor: أن كونهم مع هؤلاء تارة ومع هؤلاء تارة من الحكمة والإصلاح وهو عين الإفساد

rows.speaker: الحرالي
rows.claim: Their failure to perceive means they do not recognize how their present plotting harms themselves or what it will bring later; believers need not fear them because God will suffice against them.
rows.anchor: في أذى أنفسهم , فلا تخافوهم فإني كافيكموهم

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The people whose faith is held up as the model are true believers, with faith outwardly and inwardly; hypocrites call such believers fools for leaving their fathers' religion.
rows.anchor: { كما آمن الناس } أي الذين هم الناس ليظهر عليكم ثمرة ذلك

rows.speaker: الحرالي
rows.claim: The believers' faith is initially an act rather than an ingrained attribute; those whose faith has become an attribute scarcely engage hypocrites, who find no conversational opening with them.
rows.anchor: ولكن إيمانهم كما قال الحرالي فعل من أفعالهم لم ينته إلى أن يصير صفة لهم

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The hypocrites label believers fools because, in their view, abandoning ancestral religion for a new one shows weak judgment.
rows.anchor: الذين استدرجتهم إلى استدراجهم ما دخلوا فيه بعد ترك ما كان عليه آباؤهم

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: God reverses their charge: the hypocrites alone are fools, since they stubbornly cling to an opinion whose falsehood is as clear as daylight.
rows.anchor: لجمودهم على رأيهم مع أن بطلانه أظهر من الشمس ليس فيه لبس

rows.speaker: الحرالي
rows.claim: Their ignorance is compounded and extends beyond this issue; true knowledge is what is taken through a sign or indicator established as evidence.
rows.anchor: { ولكن لا يعلمون } أي ليس لهم علم أصلالا بذلك ولا بغيره

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The past-tense form آمنا suffices to convey the hypocrites' claim that they believe, even if the belief arose only as a transient act.
rows.anchor: معبرين بالجملة الفعلية الماضية التي يكفي في إفادتها لما سقيت له أدنى الحدوث

rows.speaker: الحرالي
rows.claim: A meeting entails some turning toward one another; believers whose faith is an established attribute rarely meet hypocrites in a way that permits intimacy or speech.
rows.anchor: وللقاء اجتماع بإقبال

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The hypocrites' private return to their leaders is expressed as going to their devils; Satan is one profoundly distant from the place of good.
rows.anchor: الذين هم رؤوسهم من غير أن يكون معهم مؤمن , والشيطان هو الذي الشديد البعد عن محل الخير

rows.speaker: الحرالي
rows.claim: Their nominal statement إنّا معكم, reinforced by emphasis, presents their allegiance as fixed and counters any suspicion that their public compliance changed their position.
rows.anchor: معبرين بالأسمة الدالة على الثبات مؤكدين لها دالالة على نشاطهم لهذا الإخبار

rows.speaker: الحرالي
rows.claim: They explain their gentleness toward believers by saying they are only mocking: mockery displays seriousness while concealing its joking intent.
rows.anchor: الهزء إظهار الجد وإخفاء الهزل فيه قاله الحرالي

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: God's mockery repays theirs through gradual enticement: they are treated outwardly as believers while being made to taste renewed humiliation in both worlds.
rows.anchor: يجازهم على فعلهم بالاستداج بأن يظهر لهم من أمره المرذي لهم

rows.speaker: الحرالي
rows.claim: The imperfect verb for God's mockery indicates renewed, continuing recompense; its verbal form also leaves room for repentance by one who repents.
rows.anchor: فلذلك عبر بالفعليه دون الاسمية

rows.speaker: الحرالي
rows.claim: مدّ means a connected increase in something of its own kind, while their طغيان is excessive transgression of boundaries in corruption.
rows.anchor: من المدد وهو مزيد متصل في الشيء من جنسه

rows.speaker: الحرالي
rows.claim: To blunder in their transgression is to lose all insight; each limit they cross leaves them confused and unable to turn back, so their transgression keeps increasing.
rows.anchor: فلا يتعدون حداإلا عمهوا فلم يرجعوا عنه فهم أبدامتزايدو الطغيان

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The buyers of misguidance persist in their desires, forcing themselves against the innate disposition God gave them despite the available evidence; they exchanged guidance, the axis of conscious good, for what is ugly.
rows.anchor: لجوا في هواهم فكلفوا أنفسهم ضد ما فطرها الله عليه مع ما نصب من الأدلة

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Their trade did not profit: they squandered their capital and retained only misguidance, which lowers its companion below animals despite their claim to discernment.
rows.anchor: أضاعوا رأس المال , لأنه لم يبق في أيدهم غير الضلال الذي صاحبة في دون رتبة البهائم

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The author says he will explain in Joseph that the twelve forms of the root ش ر ي revolve around persistence or clinging.
rows.anchor: وسيأتي في سورة يوسف عليه السلام بيان أن مادة شرى بتركيبها الاثنى عشر تدور على اللحاجة

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The inability of opponents to match the Qur'an establishes that its parables are God's speech; even worldly fruits and spouses resemble Paradise only in name and outward form, not taste, purity, or reality.
rows.anchor: فقد باينته بالطعوم والطهارة وما لا يعلمه حق علمه إلا الله تعالى

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Even the finest human sayings and parables, though remembered enduringly, cannot compare with God's examples; their lasting quality does not make them equivalent.
rows.anchor: فلم يبق إلا طعنهم بأنها لكونها بالأشياء الحقيرة لا تليق بكبريائه

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: God's use of humble creatures in examples is fitting: everything is insignificant beside divine majesty, yet omitting such comparisons would close an extraordinary means of clarifying meanings.
rows.anchor: فلو ترك التمثيل بها لذلك لانسد ذلك الباب الذي هو من أعجب العجاب

rows.speaker: الحرالي
rows.claim: Because the comprehensive call requires examples to bring understanding to the hesitant and resistant, this verse supplies a comprehensive proof that God's parables are true.
rows.anchor: وصل بها هذه الآية الجامعة لإقامة الحجة في ضرب الأمثال

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Whether measured against God or against humans, both the tiny creature used in a parable and its audience are equally weak creations; any distinction in honor comes only from God's choice.
rows.anchor: وإن اعتبر بالنسبة إليكم كان الفريقان بمنزلة واحدة في أنه خلق حقير ضعيف صغير من تراب

rows.speaker: الحرالي
rows.claim: Believers recognize that God's example is true and intended as gracious instruction that nurtures them; even sound human parables lack the unqualified truth of God's speech.
rows.anchor: حصل للذين آمنوا استبصار بنور الإيمان في ضرب المثل

rows.speaker: الحرالي
rows.claim: The disbelievers' question about what God intends by a lowly example is a scornful, ignorant, stubborn rejection of its point.
rows.anchor: استهزاء وجهلا وعنادا وجفاء

rows.speaker: الحرالي
rows.claim: The order mentioning misguidance before guidance answers the questioner who merits being led away; here misguidance means opening a path out of the saving straight road.
rows.anchor: وقدم الجواب بالإضلال لأنه مستحق المستفهم , والإضلال التطريق للخروج عن الطريق الجادة المنجية

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Those who submit to God's example are guided through it to understanding, expanded knowledge, reassurance, and increased faith; the guided are many in reality but few beside the astray.
rows.anchor: يهديهم ربهم بإيمانهم فيفهمهم المراد منه ويشرح صدورهم لما فيه من المعارف

rows.speaker: الحرالي
rows.claim: Only the morally wayward are led astray: فسق is departure from the enclosure of insight, innate disposition, covenant, and proper care, like a fruit leaving its casing.
rows.anchor: الذين خرجوا عن إحاطة الاستبصار و جهات تلقي الفطرة والعهد الموثق وحسن الرعاية

rows.speaker: الحرالي
rows.claim: The covenant is the commitment grounded in human reason and the signs God set up; its particular form is the sending of messengers, with scriptures confirming and easing reflection on it.
rows.anchor: بما ركز فيهم من العقول ونصب لهم من الدلائل

rows.speaker: الحرالي
rows.claim: A mīthāq is a firm bond; here the prophets' books confirm the covenant already brought close to human nature and made easy for reflection.
rows.anchor: بدلالة الكتب على ألسنة الرسل مع تقريبه من الفطر وتسهيله للنظر , والوثاق شدة الربط

rows.speaker: الحرالي
rows.claim: Cutting what God commands to join means severing connected innate dispositions and other goods; God commands their completion with further knowledge so they reach their fullest development.
rows.anchor: القطع الإبانة في الشيء الواحد والوصل مصيرا لتكملة مع المكمل شيئا واحدا

rows.speaker: الحرالي
rows.claim: Corruption on earth consists of putting an inferior opposite in place of what should be complete and leaving incomplete what should be perfected; the earth is where bodily and moral forms grow.
rows.anchor: { وإذا تولى سعى في الأرض ليفسد فيها ويهلك الحرث والنسل والله لا يحب الفساد }

rows.speaker: الحرالي
rows.claim: The losers diminish what should grow: across their three linked conditions they reduce their own capital, and the distant demonstrative places them far from good.
rows.anchor: والخسارة النقص فيما شأنه النماء

rows.speaker: الحرالي
rows.claim: After the invitation, examples, and responses to the evidence of divine oneness, the address turns sharply to rebuke those who persist in disbelief and to point toward release from loss through resurrection.
rows.anchor: صرف وجه الخطاب عن المواجهة من الحق تعالى وأجري على لسان لؤم وإنكار

rows.speaker: الحرالي
rows.claim: The interrogative كيف exposes the absence of any excuse for continued disbelief; because it asks about perceptible states, it challenges them about the observable conditions in which they persist.
rows.anchor: فجاء هذا الاستفهام لإيضاح انقطاع العذر في التمادي على الكفر

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The phrase about being dead, then made alive, dying, and being revived can be attached to an implied command to remember these events; the beginning already lets the thoughtful infer the return.
rows.anchor: إذ من البدءة تعلم العودة لمن تدبر

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Humanity was made for lasting life, not extinction: God created the cosmos for people, as provision, means, and support for their preservation and development.
rows.anchor: لم يخلق هذا النوع البشري للفناء بل للبقاء

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The story of Adam is a manifest example that humanity is the intended purpose of this existence and that wisdom requires resurrection to a realm without disorder, where divine wisdom is fully evident.
rows.anchor: النوع الآدمي هو المقصود بالذات من هذا الوجود

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The account displays Adam's distinction through knowledge, the angels' prostration, his residence in Paradise, and God's provision of repentance after his lapse.
rows.anchor: ثم بإسجاد الملائكة له , ثم بإسكانه الجنة , ثم بتلقي أسباب التوبة عند صدور الهفوة

rows.speaker: عبد الله بن سلام
rows.claim: A report says Muhammad is God's most honored creature; when asked about the angels, Ibn Salam says they are obedient creatures like the earth, sky, clouds, mountains, and winds, whereas Muhammad is most honored.
rows.anchor: عن بشر بن شغاف عن عبد الله بن سلام رضي الله عنه قال : ( إن أكرم خليقة الله على الله أبو القاسم

rows.speaker: البيهقي
rows.claim: Al-Bayhaqi says Ibn Salam's statement is not merely a Companion report but has the ruling of a report raised to the Prophet.
rows.anchor: وقال البيهقي : إنه ليس بموقوف بل حكمه الرفع

rows.speaker: الحرالي
rows.claim: Reason's light guides people to the signs in the visible world; prophets bring glad tidings to those who follow it and warn those distracted by worldly desires, with discourse suited to the guided and the heedless.
rows.anchor: لما جعل الله تعالى نور العقل هاديا لآيات ما ظهر في الكون

rows.speaker: الحرالي
rows.claim: The highest address is directed to Muhammad as leader of leaders; the opening الم الكتاب is an address to him and a gift from the primordial remembrance.
rows.anchor: فكان أول الخطاب ب الم ذلك الكتاب إقبالا عليه وإيتاء له من الذكر الأول

rows.speaker: رسول الله صلى الله عليه وسلم
rows.claim: The Prophet said that he was given al-Baqara and Al ʿImran from the first remembrance.
rows.anchor: كما قال عليه السلام : ( أوتيت البقرة وآل عمران من الذكر الأول )

rows.speaker: الحرالي
rows.claim: The Qur'an's final revealed material is first in the primordial record, mirroring the way the last and first are unified in God's own reality; its high address supports lower calls to the heedless.
rows.anchor: ليكون آخر المنزل الخاتم هو أول الذكر السابق

rows.speaker: الحرالي
rows.claim: The return of direct address to Muhammad reveals the unseen past of God's conversation with the angels about Adam, encouraging the guided toward higher ranks and calling the heedless back; revelation leads the rationally guided from faith to certainty.
rows.anchor: عاد وجه الخطاب إليه صلى الله عليه وسلم بما هو إعلام بغائب الماضي عن كائن الوقت

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: After mentioning Abraham's leadership, the author identifies the emulated basis of it as his religion and his testament to his sons, which they transmitted in turn, especially Jacob, the ancestor invoked by the People of Scripture.
rows.anchor: ذكر ما يؤتم به فيه وهو سبب اصطفائه وصلاحه وذلك دينه , وما أوصى به عليه السلام بنيه

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: God chose Abraham because he submitted to his Lord; the omitted object of أسلم encompasses whatever may properly be surrendered to God, and Abraham's submission is to the Lord who benefits all creation.
rows.anchor: وحذف المفعول ليتناول كل ما يصح إسلامه إلى المسلم إليه

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: وصى بها refers to Abraham's words, charge, or chosen quality; the variant وأوصى is from the same testament sense, while the doubled form more strongly conveys repeated and abundant instruction.
rows.anchor: وقرئ ( وأوصى ) فهو من إيصاء والوصية

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Abraham and Jacob tell their sons that God chose Islam for them as a mercy, sparing them the search for it; the warning means they must meet death only while wholly surrendered to God.
rows.anchor: فأغناكم عن تطلبه وإجالة الفكر فيه رحمة منه لكم

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The following verses refute the People of Scripture's claims to Judaism or Christianity by demonstrating that Abraham and the prophets were not adherents of those later religions, a falsehood they knew to be false.
rows.anchor: وبرأ خليله والأنبياء من ذلك على وجه أوجب القطع بأنهم عالمون ببطلانه

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The author gives the Torah's genealogy of Abraham through Terah and Noah, while noting that Luke's Gospel differs by inserting Cainan in the lineage.
rows.anchor: ذكر في السفر الأول منها أنه إبراهيم بن تارح بن ناحور بن شارغ

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The Torah narrative says Terah took Abram, Lot, and Sarai from Ur toward Canaan but settled in Haran; after Terah's death, God called Abram at age seventy-five to leave his land and family for the promised land and nationhood.
rows.anchor: وقال الرب لإبرم : اخرج من أرضك من حيث ولدت ومن آل أبيك إلى الأرض التي أريك

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Abram migrated with Lot and Sarai to Canaan, built altars at Shechem and Bethel, then famine drove him toward Egypt; fearing the Egyptians would kill him for Sarai, he asked her to say she was his sister, and Pharaoh took her until divine afflictions released her.
rows.anchor: فهبط إبرم إلى مصر ليسكنها لأن الجوع اشتد في الأرض

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: After leaving Egypt wealthy, Abram returned to Bethel; his and Lot's abundance made the land too small for both, and Lot chose the well-watered Jordan plain compared to God's garden and Egypt.
rows.anchor: ولم تكن تلك الأرض تسعهما كليهما لأن مواشيهما كثرت جدا

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Lot settled among the cities around Sodom, whose people were deeply sinful, while Abram stayed in Canaan; God again promised Abram all the land he could see and countless descendants, and Abram settled near Mamre and built an altar.
rows.anchor: وكان أهل سدوم أشرارا خطأة جدا

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The Torah describes four kings defeating five, taking Lot and Sodom's goods; Abram gathered 318 household men, pursued and defeated them, recovered Lot and the captives, and returned the plunder to Sodom's king.
rows.anchor: فعبى فتيانه ومولديه ثلاثمائة وثمانية عشر رجلا وسار في طلبهم

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: When Abram fears that his steward Eliezer will inherit, God promises an heir from Abram's own body and descendants as numerous as stars; Abram believes, and God covenants to give him the land.
rows.anchor: لا يرثك هذا بل ابنك الذي يخرج من صلبك فهو يرثك

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: God predicts Abram's descendants will be enslaved for four hundred years, judges their oppressor, and brings them back in the fourth generation after the Amorites' wrongdoing is complete; the covenant land stretches from Egypt to the Euphrates.
rows.anchor: فيتعبدونهم ويكدونهم أربعمائة سنة

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: After Sarai gives her Egyptian servant Hagar to Abram because she is barren, Hagar conceives and flees Sarai's harsh treatment; an angel orders her to return and promises many descendants through Ishmael, whose hand will be against everyone and everyone against him.
rows.anchor: فحبلت فقالت سرى لإبرم : أنت صاحب ظلامتي

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Ishmael is born when Abram is eighty-six; at ninety-nine God makes a covenant with him, renames him Abraham, promises nations and kings from him, and gives Canaan to his descendants.
rows.anchor: ثم ولدت هاجر لإبرم ابنا فدعا إبرم اسمه إسماعيل

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Circumcision is made the covenant's bodily sign for Abraham's household and male descendants: household males are circumcised, boys on the eighth day, and the uncircumcised are cut off for breaking the covenant.
rows.anchor: ويكون علامة العهد بيني وبينكم , وليختن كل ذكر منكم ابن ثمانية أيام

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: God renames Sarai as Sarah and promises that she will bear Isaac; Abraham laughs at the prospect because he is one hundred and Sarah ninety, then asks that Ishmael live before God.
rows.anchor: فخر إبراهيم على وجهه ضاحكا وقال في قلبه

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: God confirms Isaac as the covenant heir while granting Abraham's request for Ishmael: Ishmael will be blessed, become a great people, and father twelve princes.
rows.anchor: وقد استجبت لك في إسماعيل فباركته وكثرته وأنميته جدا جدا

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Abraham circumcises himself at ninety-nine, Ishmael at thirteen, and the household; Sarah later bears Isaac, whom Abraham circumcises on day eight, and celebrates his weaning.
rows.anchor: وكان قد أتى إسماعيل ابنه إذ اختتن ثلاث عشرة سنة

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: When Sarah demands Hagar and Ishmael's expulsion, Abraham grieves; Hagar loses her water in the wilderness, but God hears the boy, shows her a well, promises him a great people, and Ishmael grows up in Paran as an archer.
rows.anchor: فقال الله لإبراهيم : لا يشقن عليك حال الصبي وأمتك

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The Torah account appears to conflict with the sound report that Ishmael was nursing when Abraham left him at the House: the author says the later exile account may fit, while the circumcision at thirteen can be reconciled by miraculous travel to Mecca and back.
rows.anchor: وفي الحديث الصحيح ( أنه وضعه عند البيت وهو يرضع )

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The Torah's promises that all earthly peoples will be blessed through Abraham and that Ishmael's hand will be against all are clearer prophecies of Muhammad, the only descendant who fulfilled them; al-Taftazani and al-Samarqandi also noted the passage.
rows.anchor: وفيه بشارة بنبينا محمد صلى الله عليه وسلم أصرح مما ذكروه

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The opening أم has an omitted alternative: the rebuke may ask whether they were absent or present at Jacob's testament, or whether they lacked knowledge when claiming exclusive Paradise; either way, their scripture already commands the same lesson.
rows.anchor: أكنتم غائبين عن هذه الوصية من إبراهيم ويعقوب عليهما السلام أم حاضرين

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The passage warns against following ancestors merely because they are ancestors: one must obey the first Benefactor, God, even when his commands differ from ancestral practice.
rows.anchor: عدم وجوب التقيد بالآباء , وإرشاد إلى توسيع الفكر إلى المنعم الأول

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Asking whether the People of Scripture witnessed Jacob's testament challenges their claim to Paradise: were they present and obedient to his charge, or absent and without grounds for claiming it? Their scripture itself suffices to refute them.
rows.anchor: أكنتم شهداء لذلك منه حتى تكونوا ممن ائتمر بأمره في وصيته

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The question whether they were witnesses also means they have no reason to inquire into ancestors: neither lineage nor ancestral deeds benefit them, since a person has only what they themselves earn.
rows.anchor: لأنه ليس للإنسان إلا ما سعى

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Not following Abraham and Jacob in Islam severs religious kinship, which is stronger than blood kinship; the better reading is that Paradise belongs to those who submit with excellence, not exclusively to the People of Scripture.
rows.anchor: لأن نسب الدين أعظم من نسب الماء والطين

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The words ما تعبدون deliberately use ما to cover rational and non-rational objects, forcing the sons' reply to exclude worship of anything unintelligent; من would not secure that effect.
rows.anchor: ولو عبر بمن لم يفد جوابهم هذا التصريح ينفي عبادة شيء مما لا يعقل

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Jacob specifies من بعدي because a successor may act badly after a reformer's death, and because the sons' lifespans do not encompass all later time.
rows.anchor: لأن الخليفة كثيرا ما يخلف الغائب بسوء وإن كان مصلحا في حضوره

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Jacob's sons name Abraham, Ishmael, and Isaac as the one God worshiped by their father and forefathers; Ishmael is their uncle, a parallel of their father and thus figuratively a father too.
rows.anchor: وإسماعيل } لأنه عم والعم صنو الأب فهو أب مجازا { وإسحاق }

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: By saying one God and then that they submit to Him alone, the sons reject associationism and show that worship is directed to God rather than to ancestors; submission means having no choice against his command.
rows.anchor: تحقيقا للبراءة من الشرك وتسجيلا على أهل الكتاب بتحتم بطلان قولهم

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The description of worldly gain as قليل does not literally restrict it to a small amount: any worldly benefit that fails to endure into the afterlife is little by comparison.
rows.anchor: كل ما لم يثبت من خير الدنيا في الآخرة وإن جل حقيرا قال : { قليلا } هذا المراد

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The distant demonstrative marks those who concealed revelation as far from mercy, and its address to the Prophet hints that a group among his community may also prefer worldly gain.
rows.anchor: وفي خطاب النبي صلى الله عليه وسلم به إشعار بوقوع ذلك من طائفة من أمته

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Their food is literally fire in the author's account of the unseen, as those able to perceive the end already see it in the beginning; the exclusive إلا blocks reducing fire to a mere cause or metaphor.
rows.anchor: وفي ذكره بصيغة الحصر نفي لتأويل المتأول بكونه سببا

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: At Judgment God will neither speak favorably to them nor cleanse them of sin, praise them, or grow their deeds, because they hid the knowledge that would purify others and burdened people by concealing an easy path.
rows.anchor: { ولا يزكيهم } أي يطهرهم من دنس الذنوب أو يثنى عليهم أو ينمي أعمالهم

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: They traded guidance for misguidance and forgiveness for punishment; by concealing knowledge they misled many people and took on their burden as well.
rows.anchor: التي كانت تنجيهم إذا محت صغائرهم

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: ما أصبرهم can express how tenaciously they imprison themselves in the fire or how brazen they are; if figurative, it resembles threatening a rebel with a long prison sentence and heavy chains.
rows.anchor: وإذا جعلته مجازا كان مثل قولك لمن عاند السلطان

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: God sent the Book in truth, gradually to train and ease understanding; this applies to the Qur'an and Torah, whose truth is firm, so concealing it denies what God established and challenges his dominion.
rows.anchor: وهو صالح لإرادة القرآن والتوراة أي الثابت الكامل في الثبات

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Those who differ in the Book oppose its very contents, not merely disagree over interpretation; the phrase covers rejecting some rulings, affirming others, and distorting the text, placing them in a distant schism.
rows.anchor: وهذه العبارة تدل على أن الاختلاف قول بعض في الكتاب كله أو في شيء منه هو باطل

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The Companions feared division like that of the Jews and Christians, so they united Muslims around one codex; permissible variation in transmitted readings or understandings is not the condemned dispute.
rows.anchor: فجمعوهم على مصحف واحد

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Polytheist Arabs disbelieved in ignorance, whereas People of Scripture persisted in defiance despite repeated signs and Moses' long, gradual recitation of Torah; their hearts were made hard.
rows.anchor: لأن كفر المشركين عن جهل وكفر أولئك عن تعنت بعد تكرر مشاهدة الآيات

rows.speaker: أبو جعفر بن الزبير
rows.claim: Ibn al-Zubayr cautions that Quranic descriptions of Christians should not be treated as identical to descriptions of Jews; the pagans had not received prior scripture and prophetic instruction, though all three groups deviate from guidance.
rows.anchor: وقال الإمام أبو جعفر بن الزبير : ومتى بين شيء في الكتاب العزيز من أحوال النصارى فليس على ما ورد من مثله في اليهود

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The warnings group deviants as Jews, Christians, and polytheists; Muslim hypocrites resemble Jews in doubt, deceit, and mockery, while other people mirror Christian or polytheist errors by associating partners or assigning independent agency to creatures.
rows.anchor: وهم اليهود والنصارى وأهل الشرك , ويهم يلحق سائر من تنكب

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The author reviews the raised form of غير after المؤمنين and المغضوب عليهم, and allows raised زيد after إلا to be parsed as apposition or an adjective, citing grammarians and a prophetic saying about the peril of scholars, workers, and the sincere.
rows.anchor: وجوز في ما قام القوم إلا زبد , - بالرفع البدل والصفة

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The trial of meeting Jalut's army follows the river test because such danger shakes hearts, teaching people to seek well-being and recognize its worth; the Prophet's prayer after the harm at Taif exemplifies this.
rows.anchor: حثا على سؤال العافية وتعريفا بعظيم رتبتها

rows.speaker: الحرالي
rows.claim: The broad plural pronoun when the armies meet signals that most who crossed had drunk, while few abstained; the earlier plural for drinking likewise conveys the large number who drank.
rows.anchor: رد الضمير مردا عاما إيذانا بكثرة الذين اغترفوا وقلة الذين لم يطعموا

rows.speaker: الحرالي
rows.claim: طاقة is what an agent can bear without being overcome; their claim that they cannot face Jalut and his army reflects reliance on force and numbers, as in the earlier complaint about lacking wealth, whereas victory comes only from God.
rows.anchor: ففيه من نحو قولهم { ولم يؤت سعة من المال } اعتمادا على أن النصر بعدة مال أو قوة , وليس غلا بنصر الله
